prov.text: The provision for credit losses, which includes a provision for unfunded commitments, was $5.0 million and $18.5 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with $5.5 million and $44.7 million in the comparable prior-year periods. Included in the provision for credit losses for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was $27.4 million in initial provision for credit losses related to the FLIC merger. In each of the 2026 periods, the provision for credit losses reflected charge-offs, specific reserves on individually evaluated loans, organic loan growth and changing macroeconomic forecasts and conditions.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expenses
nonint.text:
Noninterest expenses totaled $55.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $58.7 million for the prior-year period. Noninterest expenses for the third quarter of 2025 included $2.9 million in merger, restructuring and exit charges. Excluding these charges, noninterest expenses were $55.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, down $0.4 million from $55.8 million in the prior-year period. Key drivers of the decrease included a $0.9 million decrease in FDIC insurance expense, a $0.4 million decrease in amortization of core deposit intangibles, a $0.2 million decrease in occupancy and equipment expenses and a $0.1 million decrease in other expenses, partially offset by a $0.5 million increase in salaries and employee benefits, a $0.3 million increase in professional and consulting expenses and a $0.2 million increase in marketing and advertising expenses.

Noninterest expenses totaled $168.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $171.6 million for the prior-year period. Noninterest expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included $2.2 million in merger, restructuring and exit charges, compared with $35.3 million in merger, restructuring and exit charges, including a $0.3 million BOLI restructuring charge, in the prior-year period.

nonop.heading: Noninterest Expenses
nonop.text:
Noninterest expenses totaled $55.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $58.7 million for the prior-year period. Noninterest expenses for the third quarter of 2025 included $2.9 million in merger, restructuring and exit charges. Excluding these charges, noninterest expenses were $55.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, down $0.4 million from $55.8 million in the prior-year period. Key drivers of the decrease included a $0.9 million decrease in FDIC insurance expense, a $0.4 million decrease in amortization of core deposit intangibles, a $0.2 million decrease in occupancy and equipment expenses and a $0.1 million decrease in other expenses, partially offset by a $0.5 million increase in salaries and employee benefits, a $0.3 million increase in professional and consulting expenses and a $0.2 million increase in marketing and advertising expenses.

Noninterest expenses totaled $168.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $171.6 million for the prior-year period. Noninterest expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included $2.2 million in merger, restructuring and exit charges, compared with $35.3 million in merger, restructuring and exit charges, including a $0.3 million BOLI restructuring charge, in the prior-year period.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Income tax expense was $11.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $16.3 million for the prior-year period. The effective tax rate was 26.0% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 28.4% for the prior-year period. The decrease in income tax expense and the effective tax rate was primarily due to lower taxable income resulting from the loss on loans held-for-sale related to the balance sheet restructuring.

Income tax expense was $41.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $18.4 million for the prior-year period. The effective tax rate was 27.4% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with 31.1% for the prior-year period. The $23.5 million increase in income tax expense was primarily due to higher pretax income, which was $152.8 million compared with $59.4 million in the prior-year period. This was partially offset by the effect of the loss on loans held-for-sale related to the balance sheet restructuring. Income tax expense for the prior-year period included a $3.0 million estimated state tax liability resulting from intercompany dividends. Excluding that charge, the effective tax rate for the prior-year period was 26.0%.

On June 30, 2026, the Company entered into an agreement committing up to $50.0 million to a renewable energy tax equity fund.

net.text: Net income available to common stockholders for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $29.9 million, compared to $39.5 million for the prior-year period. The Company’s diluted earnings per share was $0.59 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with $0.78 for the prior-year period. Results for the third quarter of 2026 include a pretax loss of $23.0 million on the transfer of loans held-for-sale. The $9.6 million decrease in net income available to common stockholders and the $0.19 decrease in diluted earnings per share resulted mainly from a $33.9 million decrease in noninterest income, primarily reflecting the $23.0 million pretax loss on the transfer of loans held-for-sale described above. This was partially offset by a $15.3 million increase in net interest income, a $5.2 million decrease in income tax expense, a $3.3 million decrease in noninterest expenses and a $0.5 million decrease in the provision for credit losses. The decrease in noninterest income also reflects $10.1 million of non-recurring income recognized in the third quarter of 2025, consisting of $6.6 million in employee retention tax credit ("ERTC") and a $3.5 million defined benefit pension plan curtailment gain.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income and Margin
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income is the difference between the interest earned on the portfolio of earning assets (principally loans and investments) and the interest paid on deposits and borrowings, which support these assets. Net interest income is presented on a tax-equivalent basis by adjusting tax-exempt income (including interest earned on tax-free loans and on obligations of state and local political subdivisions) by the amount of income tax which would have been paid had the assets been invested in taxable assets. Net interest margin is defined as net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis as a percentage of total average interest-earning assets.

Fully taxable equivalent net interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $118.5 million, an increase of $15.4 million, or 14.9%, from the prior-year period. The increase was due to a 33 basis-point widening of the net interest margin to 3.44% from 3.11%, and a 3.9% increase in average interest earning assets. The wider margin reflected a 15 basis-point increase in the yield on interest-earning assets and a 17 basis-point decrease in the average cost of deposits, including noninterest-bearing deposits.

Fully taxable equivalent net interest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $343.4 million, an increase of $93.8 million, or 37.6%, from prior-year period.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income was a net loss of $14.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with income of $19.4 million for the prior-year period. Noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 included the $23.0 million pretax loss on the transfer of loans held-for-sale described above. Noninterest income for the third quarter of 2025 included $10.1 million of non-recurring income, consisting of $6.6 million in ERTC and a $3.5 million defined benefit pension plan curtailment gain. Excluding these items, noninterest income decreased $0.8 million from the prior-year period. The decrease was mainly due to a $1.8 million decrease in net gains on equity securities, which went from a net gain of $1.7 million to a net loss of $0.2 million, and a $0.5 million decrease in deposit, loan and other income. These were partially offset by a $1.2 million increase in BOLI income, driven by death benefits recorded in the third quarter of 2026, and a $0.3 million increase in net gains on sale of loans held-for-sale, primarily SBA loans.

Noninterest income totaled $0.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $29.0 million for prior-year-period. Noninterest income for the nine months ended 2026 included the aforementioned $23.0 million pretax restructuring charge and in 2025 the $10.1 million in non-recurring gains discussed above.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
